title: What does a physical-first universe mean?
summary: ArcSecs asks whether measurable interactions, matter, fields and clocks can explain observations without treating space and time as literal material substances. The research commitments are hypotheses, not a replacement theory established by experiment.

sections.title: The distinction between a map and a mechanism
paragraphs: A coordinate system tells us where events occur and how they are related. A physical theory also needs rules that predict what changes, which quantities are conserved, and what a detector records. The book challenges the leap from a successful mathematical description to the idea of an elastic material called spacetime.

General relativity is a well-tested dynamical geometry; the phrase “fabric” is a metaphor, not a claim that a rubber sheet fills the cosmos. An alternative must recover its measured predictions or provide a better prediction with uncertainty accounted for.

sections.title: Start with measurable objects
paragraphs: Track physical state: positions relative to a reference, energy, momentum, fields and clock counts. Specify initial conditions, sources and detector calibration before interpreting a redshift or a trajectory. A label for time is not itself a measured physical clock.

The research program uses a common progression parameter T. This is a bookkeeping assumption and not an independently established universal clock. Models with different physical rates must still reproduce the same actual measurement protocols.

sections.title: A model must be able to fail
paragraphs: A diagram cannot establish a new force. Specify a null model, derive the observable, check conservation, and compare against independent data. A simulation that merely encodes a desired conclusion proves nothing about nature.

questions.q: Does ArcSecs reject relativity’s measurements?
questions.a: No. The challenge concerns physical interpretation and whether an alternative mechanism can reproduce the measurements. Established reference calculations are retained.

questions.q: Is the physical-first proposal proven?
questions.a: No. It is an independent research program with stipulated premises and conditional mathematical models.

title: The twelve foundations, explained
summary: The twelve ArcSecs premises frame the research questions. They are not twelve established experimental results; several challenge standard physics and require decisive tests.

sections.title: 1–3 · Light and time
paragraphs: 1. Photon mass: distinguish energy-equivalent mass E/c² from intrinsic invariant rest mass. Standard photons have zero invariant mass; a positive mass is an unconfirmed hypothesis.

2. Constant time: use one progression variable while investigating the physical processes that determine readings. 3. Photon slowing: measure group speed separately from energy loss; a spectral shift alone cannot establish a speed change.

sections.title: 4–7 · Where, when and physical extent
paragraphs: 4. Time is the when: ordering and measured intervals. 5. Space is the where: relative locations and geometry. 6. Physical existence: define extent, energy, momentum and mass operationally; the premise does not prove that all physical entities have rest mass. 7. Spacetime is not treated as a material substance in this research program. The mathematical success of relativistic geometry is not denied.

sections.title: 8–9 · Speed and separation
paragraphs: 8. Investigate whether any interaction can propagate locally faster than the usual light benchmark. No such controllable superluminal signal is established. 9. Investigate physical separation independently of local causality: distant recession rates can exceed c in conventional cosmology without enabling local faster-than-light communication.

sections.title: 10–12 · Cosmic inference
paragraphs: 10. The total extent of physical reality is not measured by the observable horizon alone. 11. A fitted age of our cosmic history is not the age of every hypothetical parent domain. 12. The possibility of overestimated astronomical sizes and distances is investigated with independent anchors; the direction of error is not universal.
This is a paraphrased guide. The definitive wording and the interpretation layer remain on ArcSecs; consult that charter for the original statements.

questions.q: Are the twelve statements observations?
questions.a: No. They are authorial research commitments, with separate test criteria and limitations.

questions.q: Does the charter imply the Big Bang cannot have occurred?
questions.a: No. A regional hot, dense history is compatible with investigating a larger or differently interpreted cosmos.

title: Can photons have mass?
summary: Light demonstrably carries energy and momentum. A nonzero invariant photon rest mass is a distinct, unconfirmed physical hypothesis with stringent observational and laboratory constraints.

sections.title: Energy is not invariant mass
paragraphs: A light packet can transfer momentum to a mirror or excite an atom. Those effects occur in ordinary electromagnetic theory with zero invariant photon mass. Assigning E/c² as an energy-equivalent mass does not measure rest mass.

In a positive-gap dispersion model, E² = C²p² + Eₘ². Here Eₘ is the trial rest energy, and C is a characteristic speed in the assumed medium. The group speed is C²p/E. The zero-gap limit returns C for nonzero momentum.

sections.title: What would distinguish the hypothesis?
paragraphs: A nonzero photon gap can change dispersion, electromagnetic static fields and the available polarization degrees of freedom. Each effect must be consistent with charge conservation, spectroscopy and receiver response. A frequency-dependent travel time also needs independent source timing and a specified environment.
The book’s later microscopic chapters investigate massive-vector and atomic-receiver models rather than assuming all light behaves like a classical massive ball.

sections.title: Explore the limit
paragraphs: In the photon history lab, choose a tiny rest-energy fraction. A large change in energy may create a speed deficit below ordinary floating-point resolution; the stable deficit formula is reported independently. This is one reason redshift is not direct evidence of massive photons.

questions.q: Does gravitational bending establish photon rest mass?
questions.a: No. General relativity predicts gravitational light deflection for zero-rest-mass photons.

questions.q: Is a positive photon gap established?
questions.a: No. It is a trial parameter. The lab tests its conditional effects, including recovery of the zero-gap control.

title: Can light lose energy or slow as it travels?
summary: A photon’s energy, frequency, group velocity and travel history are different observables. A physical aging mechanism needs an energy recipient, momentum accounting, optical preservation and timing predictions.

sections.title: Redshift is a measurement, not a mechanism
paragraphs: Astronomers measure a spectral ratio 1+z = λobs/λem (using consistent standards). Expansion, motion and gravity have well-established redshift predictions. A proposed propagation-loss mechanism must be tested independently, not inferred solely from a red spectrum.

The book’s CR3–CR5 control assumes a fixed gap and exponential momentum drag. It computes energy and group speed separately. Its bath ledger tracks loss but does not identify the microscopic recipient.

sections.title: Why the environment matters
paragraphs: The candidate static scalar regulator in CR1–CR2 sets a characteristic speed C(I) = C*/√(1+αI²). The thin-shell example can slow propagation near a boundary and permit reacceleration outside. That is a counterexample to automatic monotonic slowing.

A static field is not an autonomous transport mechanism. The moving source, absorber, receiver and field must exchange energy and momentum consistently. A separate gapless reference and a zero-loss run are indispensable.

sections.title: Three observational challenges
paragraphs: Energy loss alone cannot explain all observations. For stationary endpoints with identical emission and reception conditions, a stationary propagation delay is the same for each packet, so arrival intervals are not stretched. Supernova time stretching is an independent constraint.

Recoil may broaden an image; scattering, dimming and spectral noise must stay within measurements. The Review 6.0 escape and phase-matching experiments test restricted conversion channels but do not establish universal photon aging.

questions.q: Does redshift prove slowing?
questions.a: No. Even a large energy loss may cause almost no group-speed change for a tiny positive gap.

questions.q: Can a photon reaccelerate in the toy regulator?
questions.a: Yes. The static shell control has a higher characteristic speed outside the boundary. Preventing this requires an additional physical mechanism.

title: Are clocks measuring a substance called time?
summary: Clocks count physical processes. ArcSecs investigates a universal progression parameter with process-dependent rates, while conventional relativity accurately predicts measured clock differences.

sections.title: A clock is an interaction
paragraphs: An atomic clock counts cycles of a transition; a mechanical clock counts oscillations. Both report intervals by comparing a physical process to a reference. The book’s T-01/T-03 framework separates progression T from accumulated counts N = ∫ν(T)dT.

A universal progression parameter is not automatically accessible as a measured master clock. In standard relativity, proper time is the physically measured interval along a trajectory, not a material flow.

sections.title: Compare actual readings
paragraphs: In a simple constant-rate control, two clocks run for the same coordinate interval but accumulate different counts. Special relativity gives the inertial reference rate √(1−β²) in a specified frame. Gravitational shifts require the appropriate metric or weak-field approximation.
A proposed process-based alternative must explain why many different physical clocks and unstable particles agree with relativistic predictions, not just fit one atomic transition.

sections.title: Emission and reception
paragraphs: Successive light pulses can arrive farther apart because the endpoints move or because the propagation conditions evolve. A receiver’s local rate affects its measured interval. Spectral ratios and arrival intervals are separate calibration problems.

questions.q: Do slower clocks prove time is a material?
questions.a: No. They establish differences in measured proper time or clock rates; a material-substance interpretation is not required.

questions.q: Does a common T prove absolute time exists?
questions.a: No. It is a model choice that must reproduce observations and make testable distinctions.

title: Did the Big Bang happen? Can the universe expand?
summary: A hot, dense early cosmic history and physical expansion are not ruled out by ArcSecs. The speculative question is whether our observed region belongs to a larger physical system and whether different mechanisms can explain its measured evolution.

sections.title: What the standard reference explains
paragraphs: The hot Big Bang model is supported by cosmic expansion, the cosmic microwave background and primordial light-element abundances. It is not an ordinary explosion from a single point into surrounding empty space. In a homogeneous cosmology, large-scale separations are described by a changing scale factor.

The flat Friedmann reference in our lab uses radiation, matter and a cosmological constant. Changing parameters changes the predicted elapsed history; this is a calculation, not a fit to observations.

sections.title: An age is a model inference
paragraphs: The roughly 13.8-billion-year standard estimate describes the calibrated cosmic history within the standard model. A hypothetical parent cosmos or preceding phase is not measured by that estimate. The observable region is also distinct from the entire universe.
ArcSecs retains unknown total size and total age as separate premises. No evidence currently establishes neighboring bubble universes or an actual boundary surrounding our observed sky.

sections.title: Physical recession as an alternative control
paragraphs: The book explores a central linear acceleration r″ = Aₓr, giving r = r₀ cosh(√AₓT) for initially resting objects when Aₓ is positive. This increases physical separations. The model does not derive the full expansion history, redshift, CMB or nucleosynthesis.
An alternative must compare predicted distances, time stretch, BAO, CMB, element abundances and structure formation against data with shared parameters.

questions.q: Does ArcSecs deny the Big Bang?
questions.a: No. A hot, dense early history is permitted and the conventional reference remains part of the simulations.

questions.q: Is the observed horizon a physical wall?
questions.a: No known observation establishes that. A domain boundary is an extra hypothetical structure.

title: Could our universe be a bubble in a greater cosmos?
summary: The book investigates hypothetical physical domains with boundaries, pressure differences and external fields. A domain can grow or contract in a mechanical model; no neighboring cosmic domain has been established by observation.

sections.title: Define the boundary first
paragraphs: A material interface, a field-state domain wall and the observable horizon are distinct. A toy spherical interface may have surface tension σ, pressure difference ΔP and wall inertia. Its radial force is 4πR²ΔP − 8πRσ. The balance radius 2σ/ΔP is unstable for fixed positive pressure difference.
A growing wall does not automatically move the interior galaxies. A coupling to matter, an energy budget and a photon transport law are additional requirements.

sections.title: Would an exterior pull us outward?
paragraphs: An exactly spherical Newtonian exterior mass shell has zero gravitational acceleration in its cavity. A finite-range scalar with different coupling can produce a nonzero gradient; this is a separate hypothetical interaction, not ordinary gravity under a new name. A distant asymmetric mass produces tides: extension along one axis and compression across others.

A physical external influence must propagate by a specified causal mechanism and account for source recoil, field energy and momentum. The R41 model and later collision lab offer restricted computational examples, not a measured parent universe.

sections.title: Population and collision claims
paragraphs: A seeded birth–death process can illustrate domains forming and disappearing with assumed rates. It cannot derive nucleation rates or prove such domains exist. Collision searches require a specified sky signature, null injections, foreground controls, trial corrections and independent observations.
The book distinguishes the pressure force, screened-field coupling, tidal deformation and collision transfer. None should be silently conflated with another.

questions.q: Can a bubble grow without galaxies moving apart?
questions.a: Yes in a toy wall model with no interior coupling; the wall and interior motion are separate state variables.

questions.q: Do other universes definitely pull ours?
questions.a: No. A physical coupling and external source are hypothetical, and the symmetric Newtonian null control remains.

title: Are cosmic distances and sizes overestimated?
summary: ArcSecs investigates distance inference, not a universal correction. Geometry, flux, spectral shifts and time intervals are different measurements; an alternative propagation model can change the inferred distances in different directions.

sections.title: Three routes to a distance
paragraphs: Parallax estimates geometric distance from an observed angular shift and a known baseline. Luminosity distance uses calibrated luminosity and received flux; angular diameter distance uses calibrated transverse size and angular size. Standard candles, standard rulers and lensing each have their own systematics.

In a simple extinction model, dimming by A magnitudes makes an object appear farther away if extinction is ignored. The distance ratio is 10^(A/5). A different systematic can produce the opposite sign.

sections.title: A signed travel-time control
paragraphs: If an individual packet’s speed declines exponentially from c₀ to fc₀ between stationary endpoints and travel time is independently known, a constant c₀ inference overestimates distance by −ln f/(1−f). This is a special travel-time example, not a cosmological redshift law.

The book also examines globally changing characteristic histories and prescribed material outflow. Their inferred distances depend on the emission condition, receiver calibration and propagation history.

sections.title: Compare the observable relationships
paragraphs: In the Chapter 32A finite-gap benchmark, energy redshift and arrival stretch differ, and distance duality can depart from the conventional relation. This prediction is conditional on isotropic straight rays, stable clocks and specified survival.

An astronomical claim needs independent distances, calibrated fluxes, sample selection, uncertainty and comparisons with conventional cosmology. Smaller-and-closer is a research premise, not a proven universal result.

questions.q: Does ArcSecs prove all objects are closer?
questions.a: No. The book preserves signed inference errors and identifies cases requiring opposite corrections.

questions.q: Can redshift alone determine distance in an alternative model?
questions.a: Not without a specified propagation and motion model, calibration and observational fit.

title: Gravity, physical separation and causality
summary: The research seeks concrete interactions underlying gravitational observations. Gravitational light bending and clock shifts do not by themselves identify a material spacetime substance or establish an alternative force.

sections.title: A successful reference is not optional
paragraphs: General relativity predicts lensing, gravitational redshift, orbital precession and gravitational waves. Newtonian mechanics works in its appropriate weak-field, slow-motion domain. An alternative has to reproduce those successes, not discard them because of a metaphor.

The book investigates relational geometry, source-coupled fields and physical recoil. A field can store energy and momentum even when no mechanical ether is assumed. Its coupling, propagation and detector response must be specified.

sections.title: Separation speed versus local signal speed
paragraphs: A distant recession rate can exceed c in conventional cosmology; that does not let a local signal exceed light. ArcSecs separately studies coordinate separation rates, electromagnetic characteristics and possible all-sector signal propagation. No faster-than-light local communication has been established.

The Chapter 32A Galilean outflow trial can even increase common-coordinate packet speed while medium-relative speed falls. This is a limitation of that prescribed kinematics, not an observed violation of relativity.

sections.title: How to test an exterior field
paragraphs: Compare the exact Newtonian shell null against a static screened scalar trial. A real dynamic field must show delayed response and reciprocal momentum exchange. The book’s R41 numerical model is one-dimensional, with periodic boundaries and smooth source tails; it does not establish a sharp causal front or cosmic source.

questions.q: Is an exterior field the same as gravity?
questions.a: Not necessarily. A pressure gradient, tidal field and hypothetical screened interaction have different equations and predictions.

questions.q: Can recession faster than c send a local message faster than light?
questions.a: No. Distant separation rates and local causal signals are different quantities.

title: Could a dark matter drive produce thrust?
summary: The book explores a hypothetical momentum machine that would collect a physical substrate and expel reaction mass. No demonstrated dark-matter capture or propulsion mechanism exists.

sections.title: Start with mass and momentum
paragraphs: A trial intake model uses ṁ = ηρAv. Density, effective capture area, relative speed and efficiency must refer to the same frame and physical material. The resulting number is available captured mass, not thrust.
In a nonrelativistic ship-frame control, jet power is ½ṁvₑ². Incoming material carries momentum, so net axial thrust is ṁ(vₑ−vᵢ) minus other drag. A limited power budget constrains exhaust speed.

sections.title: Heat cannot be ignored
paragraphs: The engine must supply confinement and acceleration energy. Inefficiency and intake heating create a waste heat load. An ideal radiator emits εσSB A(T⁴−Tbg⁴); actual spacecraft need design margins, materials and thermal transport.
An assumed capture area may be immense, and unknown substrate coupling can make efficiency effectively zero. No mass capture means no reaction thrust from this mechanism.

sections.title: From proposal to engineering evidence
paragraphs: A credible experiment would measure captured mass, supplied power, exhaust momentum, heat and external force independently. The drive demo is exploratory; the engineering control makes its assumptions inspectable and refuses to turn hypothetical parameters into demonstrated performance.

questions.q: Is the drive a working technology?
questions.a: No. It is a conditional engineering research proposal.

questions.q: Does increasing density guarantee positive net thrust?
questions.a: No. Intake drag, exhaust power and heat can dominate. Zero capture gives zero reaction thrust.

title: What would count as evidence for Beyond Spacetime?
summary: A meaningful test separates assumptions, conditional mathematics, numerical verification and observations. The program’s claims must remain falsifiable, and failed controls must remain visible.

sections.title: Four levels of claims
paragraphs: Premise: a starting proposition, not a measurement. Conditional derivation: a mathematical consequence of specified assumptions. Numerical verification: a check that code solves those equations within tolerance. Empirical validation: independent measurements discriminate the proposed mechanism from alternatives.
A conservation residual or successful comparison to an archived simulation is numerical verification, not evidence that the modeled material exists.

sections.title: Design a fair comparison
paragraphs: Declare initial conditions, units, assumptions, uncertainties and acceptance criteria before running a model. Include an established reference and a null control. Check limiting cases, convergence, conservation and parameter degeneracies.

For cosmology, fit a calibration subset and predict an independent holdout with the same physical parameters. Do not substitute a visually persuasive animation for a quantitative likelihood or ignore observations that challenge the proposal.

sections.title: Trace the source
paragraphs: Every learning lab here has a compact input schema, equations, assumptions, numerical output and a source pointer. The complete source data, manuscripts, historical reports and extended simulations remain on ArcSecs. This site explains and demonstrates small models; it does not republish the book.

questions.q: Does a passing software test prove a hypothesis?
questions.a: No. It establishes specified software behavior, not empirical truth.

questions.q: Where can I inspect the original calculations?
questions.a: The ArcSecs research library and reproducibility center maintain the original papers, scripts, datasets and verification records.
